author: Jonathan Harrison
title: After 3 days and 12 overtimes, Minnesota youth hockey game finally ends - NewsBreak
text:
By Jonathan Harrison ,
4 hours ago
Incredible scenes have played out on hockey sheets throughout the world over the past couple of days, including a marathon game that took three days to complete in Minnesota youth hockey.
A U-12 girls game between Cottage Grove and St. Paul started Monday night and didn't end until 12 overtimes forced the game into a shootout, which was completed on Wednesday night.
The matchup was suspended after six overtimes at 10:45 p.m. on Monday, with the game tied 1-1.¬†The game resumed Tuesday but was again halted with the score still deadlocked after four additional scoreless overtime periods.
The teams returned to Doug Woog Arena in South St. Paul on Wednesday, and after they stayed tied through the 11th and 12th overtimes ‚Äî they even played 3-on-3 in the 12th overtime ‚Äî the game went to a shootout, where Cottage Grove finally found a way to break the tie and win.
Not only that, but they had to change the rules to go to a shootout after 15 periods failed to settle it.
In all, the game lasted roughly 6 1/2 hours and there were a combined 153 shots on goal 97 for St. Paul, 56 for Cottage Grove), according to the box score .
Hermantown domination In the Class 1A, Section 7 matchup between Hermantown and North Shore, an incredible 70 shots were recorded between the two teams. However, only one of the shots came from North Shore, which was outshot 69-1 by the powerhouse Hawks on¬† Tuesday.
Hermantown, the No. 2 seed in the section, dominated with four goals in the opening period and 10 more in the second period.
Bode Madill and Beau Christy both finished with five points. Madill led all scorers with three goals, adding two assists. Christy was one of four Hawks to record three assists.
Next up for Hermantown, as they look to qualify for the state tournament, is a showdown with No. 3 seed Cloquet/Esko/Carlton on Saturday.
Day 1 at the girls' state hockey tournament Defending Class A state champion Dodge County advanced to the semifinals on Wednesday with a 3-2 overtime victory over Proctor/Hermantown.
Dodge County, seeded fourth, will face No. 1 Warroad, which overpowered No. 8 Luverne 5-1, in the semifinals on Friday.
On the other side of the bracket, No. 2 Breck blasted No. 7 St. Cloud 8-2. They'll face the winner of the 3/6 matchup between Blake and Mankato East.
The Class AA state tournament begins on Thursday at Grand Casino Arena in St. Paul.
